top_signals.title: Permian Growth Turns Moderate Despite War
top_signals.summary: Crude oil production in the most prolific basin in the United States has remained moderate despite the war premium that pushed prices to over $100 a barrel. For some, however, the very fact of production growth in the Permian is a surprise. The Permian has been the engine driving U.S. crude oil output growth for over a decade. Annual growth in the past consistently exceeded 1 million barrels--until 2020, when pandemic lockdowns killed demand and plunged U.S. crude into negative territory briefly.
